---
title: "RAG with raghilda"
callout-appearance: simple
---

[raghilda](https://posit-dev.github.io/raghilda/) is a Python package for building and searching knowledge stores.
It takes care of the preparation side of [RAG](RAG.qmd): reading documents, splitting them into chunks, embedding those chunks, and retrieving the most relevant ones for a query.
chatlas takes care of the conversation side.
To connect the two, you write a Python function that searches the raghilda store and returns the matching passages, which you then either add to the chat input yourself or register as a tool that the model can call.

## Create store {#create-store}

A raghilda store is a database that holds your document chunks along with their embeddings.
The `DuckDBStore` backend keeps everything in a single local file, so there's no server to run.
As in the [RAG](RAG.qmd) article, let's assume you have a directory (`data`) of Markdown files that you want to use as trusted content.
This snippet reads each file, chunks it, embeds the chunks, and writes them to a store on disk:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingOpenAI
from raghilda.read import read_as_markdown
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="knowledge.db",
    embed=EmbeddingOpenAI(),
    overwrite=True,
)

chunker = MarkdownChunker()
for path in Path("data").glob("*.md"):
    doc = read_as_markdown(str(path))
    store.upsert(chunker.chunk(doc))

store.build_index()
```

`MarkdownChunker` splits each document into overlapping chunks at natural boundaries (headings, paragraphs, and sentences), and each chunk remembers the headings it falls under.
The final `build_index()` call builds two indexes: a vector index for semantic search and a BM25 index for keyword search.
Since the store is written to `knowledge.db` as you go, there's no separate step to save it.
You build it once, and your app connects to it later.


## Retrieve content {#retrieve-content}

With the store on disk, you can implement `retrieve_trusted_content()`, the function that fetches relevant content for a user query:

```python
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.connect("knowledge.db", read_only=True)

def retrieve_trusted_content(query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> list[str]:
    chunks = store.retrieve(query, top_k=top_k)
    return [f"<excerpt>{chunk.text}</excerpt>" for chunk in chunks]
```

The store remembers which embedding model it was created with, so `connect()` restores it for you and queries are embedded the same way as the documents were.
Opening the store with `read_only=True` is a good habit in an app that only retrieves content.

By default, `retrieve()` runs a hybrid search that combines semantic similarity with BM25 keyword matching.
Semantic search finds passages that mean the same thing as the query even when they use different words, while keyword search catches exact terms (like function names or error messages) that embeddings can miss.
The `top_k` limit applies to each kind of search before the results are combined, so you may get back a slightly different number of chunks than you asked for.
Overlapping chunks from the same document are also merged into one passage, so the model doesn't see the same text twice.
